proof_summary: Write the numerator valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}\lfloor m/q^i\rfloor^2\) and the denominator valuation as \(\sum_{i\ge1}G(\lfloor m/q^i\rfloor)\), where \(G(M)=\sum_{r=1}^M r\lfloor M/r\rfloor\); the bound \(G(M)\le M^2\) also establishes exact divisibility. For \(m=np+k\) with \(k<p\), every \(\lfloor m/p^i\rfloor\) for \(i\ge1\) equals \(\lfloor np/p^i\rfloor\), so both numerator and denominator valuations—and hence their difference, the quotient valuation—are unchanged.
